name: terms-update-gate
title: Terms update gate
description: A re-consent gate for changed legal text: what changed in plain lines, the full documents, one unticked box, and a Continue that says why it waits.
docs: effectiveDate is when the new terms apply (a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp, written with locale and timeZone, default en-US and UTC; a date-only string such as 2026-12-01 is a calendar day and is written as that day in any zone) and versionLabel names the version in a chip. changes is three to five plain sentences, { text, href?, linkLabel? }; an href adds a link after the sentence. documents is the list of { label, href } links to the full text, which open in new tabs so the gate stays where it is. excerpt (any markup) adds a box that scrolls, named by excerptTitle, with its scrollbar always drawn and a ring around the box while it has the keyboard focus. The consent box starts unticked and cannot start any other way. Continue is aria-disabled until it is ticked but stays reachable: pressing it early moves the focus to the box, marks it invalid, and a line under the buttons says why in words. onAccept() records the consent and may return a promise (the button is busy while it runs; a rejection shows a message and keeps the tick). Once it resolves the card shows Thank you, you are all set, says it politely and moves the focus to it, and onAccepted runs acceptedDelay ms later (default 1200), so a screen reader has spoken before the page changes: navigate there, not in onAccept. onDecline() is a button of the same size as Continue, next to a note saying what declining does. defaultDone starts on the accepted state for a preview; footer, titleAs and labels (every word, with {date}) work as in the other auth cards.
